{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent history, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment-driven momentum.",
    "If model forecast is rising sharply after a recent dip, it often overshoots — cap upward trend at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust based on sentiment lag.",
    "When true outcome shows strong upward breakout (e.g., >80) from low base, model often fails to capture early momentum — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent range if sentiment is neutral or positive.",
    "If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and model is rising, it often overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect mean reversion or lack of bullish sentiment.",
    "Model tends to underestimate true outcome when sentiment is flat (0.00) and recent price is rising — apply a 1–3% upward bias to forecast if price is trending up.",
    "If model forecast is flat or slightly rising while true outcome is volatile, consider smoothing forecast to avoid overfitting to recent noise — especially if sentiment is low or mixed.",
    "After a spike in sentiment (e.g., 0.50), model often fails to adjust downward — if true outcome reverses, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect sentiment decay or mean reversion.",
    "If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by 2–5% over 3–5 days, consider applying a ‘sentiment-adjusted upward bias’ — especially if sentiment is positive or neutral."
  ]
}
